subject: English
passage: Though Victoria Vogt, author of the poetry collection Quiet Apertures, is perhaps not as widely read as the most celebrated American poets of the past half-century, influential figures have championed her work, including the poet Reynold Hayes and the literary critic Jacques Murphy. In his introductory essay to Vogt's collection, Murphy praises its deft fusion of what the aesthetician Karl Rothe called the contemplative and declarative registers—while Rothe insisted that poems could be classified as either contemplative (privileging interior reflection) or declarative (privileging public assertion), Quiet Apertures demonstrates that a poem can be both.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain what inspired a poet to write a particular collection.
choices.B: To present a reason why a literary critic is impressed by a certain collection of poems.
choices.C: To compare the work of a poet with the work of another poet who admired her.
choices.D: To argue that all poetry must be classified as belonging to one of two categories.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer because it most accurately describes the main purpose of the text, which is to present a reason why literary critic Jacques Murphy is impressed by Victoria Vogt's collection Quiet Apertures. After briefly introducing Vogt and noting that influential figures such as Murphy have championed her work, the text focuses on Murphy's introductory essay and explains that he praises the collection for fusing what the aesthetician Karl Rothe called the contemplative and declarative registers—modes Rothe had insisted were mutually exclusive. Murphy's admiration rests on Vogt's ability to show that a poem can be both at once.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect because although the text mentions that the poet Reynold Hayes admired Vogt's work, it does not compare Vogt's poetry to Hayes's. Rather, Hayes is cited only as an example of an influential figure who has championed Vogt, after which the text concentrates exclusively on Murphy's response to Quiet Apertures.
